Practised finding tens partners that make 100.
Vihaan correctly gave 40 + 60 and 80 + 20, explaining with tens.
Practised jumps of 1 and 10 on a number line.
For 65 to 100, they counted 5 first, then needed support with the remaining jumps.
The jump-of-10 meaning was still mixed up at the end; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised making 100 with tens and using jumps of 1 and 10. Vihaan used the tens idea well for 40 + 60 and 80 + 20, and explained 80 to 100 as two jumps of 10. They mixed up a jump of 10 with moving to the next number or next ten, and this was not corrected by the last example. At home, draw a number line from 65 and mark 65→70 as 5, then use separate 10-jump arrows: 70→80→90→100.
